name: Talisman of Corruption
summary: In Darkshore, Xabraxxis turns the Blackwood furbolgs against their former allies with the Talisman of Corruption. He keeps it in his personal pouch, and its magic binds the tribe to fel madness.

sections.title: A Conduit of Madness
sections.body: In Auberdine, the night elves seek the cause of the Blackwood furbolgs’ turn against their former allies. Thundris Windweaver found that satyrs brought about the tribe’s fall. Talismans like this carry corrupting sorcery through the wilderness. They taint food and twist peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. Their fel magic grips the minds and wills of local tribes.

sections.title: Breaking the Grip
sections.body: To draw out Xabraxxis, you cleanse samples of furbolg food with blessed moonwell water. The purification enrages the overseer. When Xabraxxis is slain, his demon bag yields the talisman. You bring it to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, where the Kaldorei can neutralize its foul emanations and study how to undo the demonic affliction in the forest.

faq.q: What is the Talisman of Corruption?
faq.answer: Xabraxxis uses the Talisman of Corruption to channel foul magic through the Blackwood furbolgs’ food and minds in Darkshore.

aliases: where to find talisman of corruption
faq.answer: Xabraxxis, the satyr overseeing the northern Blackwood furbolg camp near the Cliffspring River, carries the talisman in his demon bag.

faq.q: How do you draw out the owner of the talisman?
faq.answer: You gather the furbolgs’ fruit, grain, and nuts, then mix them with moonwell water in a cleansing bowl. Place the offering by the bonfire near the river. The cleansing enrages Xabraxxis until he attacks.

faq.q: What happens to the talisman after it is recovered?
aliases: who do i give the talisman to
faq.answer: You bring the talisman to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. He secures it for disposal and studies how to free the furbolgs permanently from demonic corruption.

angles.text: As a Kaldorei of Auberdine, recovering the talisman helps free your ancestral furbolg allies from demonic degradation and heal the land.
As a druid, you see devices like the talisman as a perversion of the natural order. They twist sacred beasts into feral pawns of the Burning Legion’s leftover minions.
